title: Continuous supported division from homogeneous division
statement:
Let $L$ be a field [def-weil-field], $A=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ and $\mathfrak m=(X)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Fix finitely many distinct ordered orthant vertices $\alpha_i$, put $D=\bigcup_i(\alpha_i+\mathbf N^n)$, $d_i=|\alpha_i|$, and $\Delta_i=\{\beta:\alpha_i+\beta\notin\bigcup_{j<i}(\alpha_j+\mathbf N^n)\}$. Let $f_i\in A$ have order $d_i$, and let $H_i$ be their degree-$d_i$ homogeneous parts. Assume that in every degree $t$ the indexed family
$$\{X^\beta H_i:\beta\in\Delta_i,\ |\beta|+d_i=t\}\ \amalg\ \{X^\gamma:\gamma\notin D,\ |\gamma|=t\}$$
is an $L$-basis of the degree-$t$ homogeneous polynomials. Then every $f\in A$ has a unique division
$$f=\sum_i q_i(f)f_i+r(f),\qquad \operatorname{supp}q_i(f)\subseteq\Delta_i,\quad \operatorname{supp}r(f)\subseteq\mathbf N^n\setminus D.$$
The maps $q_i,r$ are $L$-linear and continuous for the $\mathfrak m$-adic filtrations; $f\in\mathfrak m^t$ implies $q_i(f)\in\mathfrak m^{\max(0,t-d_i)}$ and $r(f)\in\mathfrak m^t$. In particular the space of supported sums $\sum_iq_if_i$ is the closed subspace $\ker r$. For any ideal $I\subseteq A$ containing all the $f_i$, use vector-space dimension [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] and put $H_I(t)=\dim_L A/(I+\mathfrak m^{t+1})$ and $H_D(t)=\#\{\gamma\notin D:|\gamma|\le t\}$. Then $H_I(t)\le H_D(t)$ for every $t$, and $H_I=H_D$ if and only if $r(f)=0$ for all $f\in I$. These assertions also hold for every degree prefix with its own orthant diagram and quotient supports whose initial forms satisfy the same basis hypothesis in every degree, and for the empty vertex family.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), 207--302, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, printed p.263; continuity is the order estimate of Lemma 7.3. Supporting route: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94. No Stacks tag states this formal division result.

proof.text: Use the coefficient-family and finite-convolution definition [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The exponents of degree at most $k$ form a finite set, since all coordinates are at most $k$. Write $g_{[k]}$ for the finite polynomial consisting of the degree-$k$ coefficients of $g$. A series lies in $\mathfrak m^k$ exactly when its coefficients of degree below $k$ vanish: one implication follows by multiplying $k$ variables; for the other, assign each exponent $\gamma$ of degree at least $k$ a fixed subexponent $\delta\le\gamma$ of degree $k$ and group its term into $X^\delta h_\delta$. There are finitely many such $\delta$, so this is an actual finite expression in the generators of $\mathfrak m^k$. For $k=0$ take $\delta=0$; for $n=0,k>0$ there are no such exponents and the series is zero.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94 (resolution context only); agent-written homogeneous coefficient recursion and finite-jet argument. BM 1997, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, p.263, is WANTED, not read.

proof.text: For each $k$, the assumed indexed basis gives unique homogeneous polynomials $u_{i,k}$ and $v_k$ for any homogeneous polynomial $P$ of degree $k$, with $P=\sum_i u_{i,k}H_i+v_k$, $u_{i,k}$ supported in $\Delta_i$ and homogeneous of degree $k-d_i$, and $v_k$ supported outside $D$ and homogeneous of degree $k$. Set $u_{i,k}=0$ if $k<d_i$. Indeed take the basis coordinates of $P$ and group the finitely many coordinates indexed by $(i,\beta)$ into $u_{i,k}$; group the other coordinates into $v_k$. Uniqueness is exactly uniqueness of coordinates in this indexed basis. No leading-monomial assumption or division theorem is being inferred here.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94 (resolution context only); agent-written homogeneous coefficient recursion and finite-jet argument. BM 1997, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, p.263, is WANTED, not read.

proof.text:
Define $E_0=f$. At stage $k$, apply Step 2 to $(E_k)_{[k]}$, obtaining $u_{i,k},v_k$, and define
$$E_{k+1}=E_k-\sum_i u_{i,k}f_i-v_k.$$
The induction invariant is $E_k\in\mathfrak m^k$ and $E_k=f-\sum_{s<k}(\sum_i u_{i,s}f_i+v_s)$. It holds at $k=0$, with the sum empty. Thus the prescription is ordinary recursion on $\mathbf N$, using only a finite coordinate calculation at each stage.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94 (resolution context only); agent-written homogeneous coefficient recursion and finite-jet argument. BM 1997, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, p.263, is WANTED, not read.

proof.text: To verify the inductive step, $f_i-H_i$ has no coefficients in degrees at most $d_i$. By the convolution formula [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $u_{i,k}(f_i-H_i)$ has no coefficients in degrees at most $k$. Hence $\sum_i u_{i,k}f_i+v_k$ has no terms below $k$, and its degree-$k$ component is $\sum_i u_{i,k}H_i+v_k=(E_k)_{[k]}$. Subtraction gives $E_{k+1}\in\mathfrak m^{k+1}$. The other invariant follows by appending the new finite summand. This proves both invariants for every $k$.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94 (resolution context only); agent-written homogeneous coefficient recursion and finite-jet argument. BM 1997, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, p.263, is WANTED, not read.

proof.text: Define $q_i$ and $r$ as coefficient families [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]: the coefficient of $q_i$ at $\beta$ is the coefficient of $u_{i,|\beta|+d_i}$ there, and the coefficient of $r$ at $\gamma$ is that of $v_{|\gamma|}$ there. These definitions require no infinite-sum existence theorem: a formal series is precisely an arbitrary coefficient family. They give $\operatorname{supp}q_i\subseteq\Delta_i$ and $\operatorname{supp}r\subseteq\mathbf N^n\setminus D$.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94 (resolution context only); agent-written homogeneous coefficient recursion and finite-jet argument. BM 1997, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, p.263, is WANTED, not read.

proof.text: Fix a degree bound $N$. A component $u_{i,k}f_i$ has no terms below $k$, so components with $k>N$ do not affect any coefficient of degree at most $N$. More explicitly, in the convolution for the coefficient at $\gamma$, a nonzero factor from $f_i$ has degree at least $d_i$, so the factor from $q_i$ has degree at most $|\gamma|-d_i$ and comes from $u_{i,k}$ with $k\le|\gamma|$. Thus $\sum_iq_if_i+r$ agrees through degree $N$ with $\sum_{k\le N}(\sum_i u_{i,k}f_i+v_k)$. The invariant says the latter agrees with $f$ through degree $N$. Coefficient equality for all $N$ gives $f=\sum_iq_if_i+r$ by [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94 (resolution context only); agent-written homogeneous coefficient recursion and finite-jet argument. BM 1997, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, p.263, is WANTED, not read.

proof.text: For uniqueness subtract two supported divisions, writing $0=\sum_i a_i f_i+b$. If this tuple is nonzero, its nonzero coefficients give a nonempty set of natural-number weights: $|\beta|+d_i$ for a coefficient of $a_i$ and $|\gamma|$ for one of $b$. Let $k$ be the least weight. Write $g^{(j)}$ for the degree-$j$ homogeneous part. In the degree-$k$ convolution [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], a homogeneous component $(a_i)^{(e)}$ vanishes if $e+d_i<k$, while $(f_i)^{(k-e)}$ vanishes if $e+d_i>k$. Thus only $e=k-d_i\ge0$ contributes, and the equation is $0=\sum_{i:d_i\le k}(a_i)^{(k-d_i)}H_i+b^{(k)}$. Its coordinates are those of the assumed degree-$k$ indexed basis because the tuple has the prescribed supports. Independence makes every such coordinate zero, although the definition of $k$ supplies a nonzero one. This contradiction proves that the tuple is zero. The argument includes $d_i=0$ and needs neither finite support of a series nor an actual least monomial equal to $\alpha_i$.

proof.text: Adding the supported divisions of $f$ and $g$ gives a supported division of $f+g$, since the support constraints are preserved by addition. Multiplying the supported division of $f$ by $c\in L$ gives one of $cf$. Uniqueness therefore implies $q_i(f+g)=q_i(f)+q_i(g)$, $q_i(cf)=cq_i(f)$ and the analogous identities for $r$, including $q_i(0)=r(0)=0$. These are $L$-linear maps.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94 (resolution context only); agent-written homogeneous coefficient recursion and finite-jet argument. BM 1997, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, p.263, is WANTED, not read.

proof.text: Suppose $f\in\mathfrak m^t$. For $k<t$, induction in the recursion gives $E_k=f$ and $u_{i,k}=v_k=0$: the degree-$k$ component of $f$ is zero, whose coordinates in a basis are all zero. Consequently $r$ has no terms below $t$ and $q_i$ has no term $X^\beta$ with $|\beta|+d_i<t$. By Step 1 these assertions say $r(f)\in\mathfrak m^t$ and $q_i(f)\in\mathfrak m^{\max(0,t-d_i)}$, with no restriction needed when $t\le d_i$.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94 (resolution context only); agent-written homogeneous coefficient recursion and finite-jet argument. BM 1997, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, p.263, is WANTED, not read.

proof.text: The $\mathfrak m$-adic topology has basic neighbourhoods $g+\mathfrak m^a$. For a target exponent $a$, the preceding bounds give $r(\mathfrak m^a)\subseteq\mathfrak m^a$ and $q_i(\mathfrak m^{a+d_i})\subseteq\mathfrak m^a$. Linearity then gives the same containments for differences at every $g$. Thus the maps are continuous for exactly the filtrations in the statement, including a constant divisor with $d_i=0$.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94 (resolution context only); agent-written homogeneous coefficient recursion and finite-jet argument. BM 1997, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, p.263, is WANTED, not read.

proof.text: Let $S$ be the space of sums $\sum_i a_if_i$ with $\operatorname{supp}a_i\subseteq\Delta_i$. Such a tuple with remainder zero is a supported division, so uniqueness gives $S\subseteq\ker r$. Conversely the division of an element of $\ker r$ expresses it as such a sum; hence $S=\ker r$. This is a closed subspace: if $r(g)\ne0$, choose a nonzero coefficient of degree $b$; for $h-g\in\mathfrak m^{b+1}$ the order bound makes that coefficient of $r(h)-r(g)$ zero. The open neighbourhood $g+\mathfrak m^{b+1}$ therefore avoids $\ker r$. Linearity supplies the subspace assertion. No closedness of an arbitrary ideal is used.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94 (resolution context only); agent-written homogeneous coefficient recursion and finite-jet argument. BM 1997, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, p.263, is WANTED, not read.

proof.text: Let $V_t$ have the finite monomial basis $X^\gamma$ for $\gamma\notin D$, $|\gamma|\le t$, of cardinality $N=H_D(t)$. Its natural map $p_t:V_t\to A/(I+\mathfrak m^{t+1})$ is surjective: division gives $f-r(f)\in I$ because every $f_i\in I$, and truncating $r(f)$ beyond degree $t$ changes it by an element of $\mathfrak m^{t+1}$. Thus its $N$ indexed monomial images span the quotient. To obtain a basis, if the current finite list has a nontrivial relation, choose a nonzero coefficient and invert it by [def-weil-field]; solve for that image in terms of the others and delete it. The remaining list still spans and has one fewer entry. Induction on the list length ends at an independent spanning list, including the empty list for the zero space. Both spaces are therefore finite-dimensional before applying [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]; it gives $\dim V_t=N$ and defines $H_I(t)$ as the quotient basis cardinality. Apply [lem-sfb-independent-family-spanning-cardinality] to that basis and the original spanning set of at most $N$ images to obtain $H_I(t)\le H_D(t)$.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94 (resolution context only); agent-written homogeneous coefficient recursion and finite-jet argument. BM 1997, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, p.263, is WANTED, not read.

proof.text: If $H_I(t)=N$, then $p_t$ is injective. Otherwise a nonzero element of its kernel gives a nontrivial relation between the $N$ indexed monomial images. Choose a nonzero coefficient; it is invertible by [def-weil-field], so that image is a combination of the other $N-1$ images. Those images span the quotient. Apply [lem-sfb-independent-family-spanning-cardinality] to a basis and this spanning set, obtaining $H_I(t)\le N-1$, a contradiction (dimension counts basis elements by [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]). If $N=0$, $V_t=0$ is already injective and there is no nonzero kernel vector to choose.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94 (resolution context only); agent-written homogeneous coefficient recursion and finite-jet argument. BM 1997, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, p.263, is WANTED, not read.

proof.text: Assume $H_I(t)=H_D(t)$ for all $t$ and take $f\in I$. Its division gives $r(f)=f-\sum_iq_i(f)f_i\in I$. Let $r_{\le t}$ be its truncation through degree $t$. It belongs to $V_t$ and to $I+\mathfrak m^{t+1}$, since $r(f)-r_{\le t}\in\mathfrak m^{t+1}$. Step 13 therefore makes $r_{\le t}=0$. For any exponent $\gamma$ take $t=|\gamma|$; its coefficient in $r(f)$ is zero. Thus $r(f)=0$ for every $f\in I$.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94 (resolution context only); agent-written homogeneous coefficient recursion and finite-jet argument. BM 1997, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, p.263, is WANTED, not read.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $r$ vanishes on $I$. For $v\in V_t$ the tuple with every quotient zero and remainder $v$ is a supported division, so $r(v)=v$. If $p_t(v)=0$, write $v=h+w$ with $h\in I$ and $w\in\mathfrak m^{t+1}$. Linearity and the order bound yield $v=r(v)=r(w)\in\mathfrak m^{t+1}$. But $v$ is a polynomial of degree at most $t$, so Step 1 forces $v=0$. Thus the $N$ monomial images are independent as well as spanning; by [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] they are a basis and $H_I(t)=N=H_D(t)$ for every $t$.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94 (resolution context only); agent-written homogeneous coefficient recursion and finite-jet argument. BM 1997, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, p.263, is WANTED, not read.

proof.text: For a degree prefix, replace the finite vertex family, $D$ and the $\Delta_i$ by those of that prefix. Under its separately stated homogeneous basis hypothesis, Steps 1--15 apply verbatim: none used a vertex outside the chosen family. This does not infer the prefix hypothesis from the full-family hypothesis. For an empty family $D=\varnothing$, the recursion has $v_k=f_{[k]}$, so $r=\mathrm{id}$ and $S=0$. The same finite-jet arguments show $H_I=H_D$ exactly when $I=0$: if $I$ contains a nonzero series, choose a nonzero coefficient of degree $t$; its truncation through degree $t$ is a nonzero vector in $V_t$ killed by $p_t$, contradicting Step 13 under equality. Conversely $I=0$ leaves all finite monomial jets independent. For $n=0$ there is only the degree-zero monomial: the empty family gives $r=\mathrm{id}_L$; a nonempty distinct vertex family can contain only $\alpha=0$, and its basis hypothesis gives a nonzero scalar divisor, $q=f/f_1$, $r=0$, and $I=L$. These verify all degenerate cases.
